- **ROUTED TO USER (new questions, per directive 1):** #10 — persona/scenario coverage: add a minimizing-non-crisis persona and/or somatic-presentation-masks-mood-disorder persona (dialogue-only cells, no modality cross; new persona authoring = DATASET-003 extension + golden labels), or explicitly descope with rationale (Finding 1). #11 — RAG ontology has no chronic alcohol-use-disorder entry (only acute intoxication/withdrawal), structurally unreachable for the VP-003 comorbidity pattern independent of the risk-lexicon filter: add an AUD ontology/corpus entry (data + DB-handoff, DATASET-005-style addendum) or accept as disclosed scope limit (Finding 3).

**Status (2026-07-10, step 5b COMPLETE — REV-022 disposition; plan v1.1 amendments):** critic verdict: **NON-BLOCKING for user presentation** (0 fully-blocking, 2 blocking-scoped, 9 major, 5 minor); no directive-1/2 violation found. Orchestrator ADOPTS all REV-022 resolutions as binding plan amendments:
1. **Pre-registered A/B adjudication rule (REV-022) adopted as BINDING for W7/W8**, verbatim: precondition (N fixed + N-scope answered, before W4) → Gate 0 (policy-B certification; FAIL → Policy A by default, B filed as future work) → Gate 0.5 (judge boolean-decision unanimity across N=3; allocation must cover ≥2 VPs, 1 crisis-adjacent + 1 non-crisis; any 2/3 split disqualifies B) → Criterion 1 safety-dominant (1a zero-tolerance shipped-evidence disqualification; 1b MET-8 incidence delta, THRESHOLD_1b fixed by data from pilot cells pre-W7) → Criterion 2 disagreement-subset top-1/top-3 (winner needs ≥2-case ABSOLUTE margin) → Criterion 3 latency tie-break only (THRESHOLD_3 by experiment-tracker pre-W7) → tie/insufficient default = **Policy A**. Certification-batch data NEVER pooled into adjudication measurements. Post-hoc criteria/threshold changes forbidden (new considerations = new REV/VAL + explicit ADR).
2. **Issues 9/10 (blocking-scoped, gate W4 only):** ADOPTED as binding design conditions — Policy A's fallback must de-risk `chief_complaint`/HPI-SOURCED query content DIRECTLY (VAL-010's actual 7-batch residual channel per REV-011 §2 — probe-turn exclusion alone re-solves an already-solved sub-problem); Policy B's judge exclusion must NAME cc/HPI content (not only `risk_assessment`), and the judge's full-transcript visibility is pre-registered here as a KNOWN, DISCLOSED exposure caught by the shared output-query risk-lexicon filter + mandatory `retrieval_meta.queries`/MET-8 audit. Both conditions land in the W4 developer brief.
3. **Issue 6 answered now (orchestrator ruling):** N is Policy A's trigger condition AND the disclosed ground-truth referent for contingency-table scoring — Policy B's judge is scored against a threshold it never sees, and every A/B write-up must state this.
4. **Owner assignments:** data — N (empirical: low percentile of cc+HPI combined `len()` distribution over EXP-008/009/011/012 clean runs; addendum to this entry, cited by commit, before W4) + THRESHOLD_1b (pre-W7) + MET-1 partial-credit rule and carried-slot scoring disposition (Issues 7/12, pre-W7). experiment-tracker — SC-2/SC-3 n restated explicitly: **n=2/VP** (SC-3: 8 F1 sessions, 16 F2; SC-2: 8 F2 replays — per its own step-3 table); SC-3b allocation FIXED = 3×VP-003 + 3×VP-001 (Issue 3); SC-3 truncation-confound caveat binding on any judge-quality claim (Issue 2); n=2/VP thin-evidence caveat (REV-018 §2) mandatory in every A/B-decision-facing write-up (Issue 4).
5. **Issue 7/8/11/16 adoptions:** carried-vs-freshly-grounded distinction pre-declared in every slot-reading metric (DATASET-006 + MET-1); the reveal-partition spec must restate DATASET-004's open circularity caveat (item b) as binding on all session-2+ correctness claims (blind authorship ≠ independent-source authorship — disclosed); A5 hereby cites REV-011 §4 option 5's HOLD as DISCHARGED (its condition met by EXP-008/EXP-011); B2's standing rule extended: **production code must never read the session ledger** (data artifact named alongside harness code).
Plan v1.1 = folded plan v1 + step-5a CVR disposition + these amendments. Steps 1–5 complete; step 6 (handoff/STATE/report) proceeding.

## [CVR-001] Plan-stage clinical-adequacy review of PLAN-2026-W28-O folded program plan v1 | 2026-07-10 | clinical-validator

**Target:** PLAN-2026-W28-O — folded program plan v1 (step 4, sections A–D, `discussion.md` "FOLDED PROGRAM PLAN v1" block); informed by DATASET-003 (VP-001~004 personas), DATASET-004 (golden domain labels), and EXP-012 (`result.md`, prior F1→F2 fresh-chain batch — the best available picture of actual dialogue/slot/RAG-candidate behavior, read as background, not re-adjudicated).
**Verdict:** adequate-with-findings (0 blocking, 6 major, 3 minor)
**Linked:** PLAN-2026-W28-O, REV-019, REV-020, EXP-012, DATASET-003, DATASET-004, DATASET-005, ADR-018, ADR-020

This is the clinical-adequacy lens's first activation (directive 3, third BINDING USER DIRECTIVE in PLAN-2026-W28-O). Overall: the plan's core clinical scaffolding is sound — the 12-slot schema is PRD-asserted 1:1 against a standard psychiatric intake structure (`docs/ai/PRD_task1_v2.md:464`: "임상 문진 표준 구조(주호소/현병력/과거력/가족력/사회력/물질사용/MSE/위험평가/평가/계획)와 1:1 대응한다"), the non-diagnostic labeling discipline is correctly carried through (`similarity_score`, `is_diagnostic: Literal[False]`), and the plan already earmarks several clinically material scenario classes (SC-5 session-1-denied-risk re-probe, SC-6 OCR-contradicts-speech non-adherence, SC-9 turn-0 crisis compound, SC-10 risk-lexicon document content). No finding below rises to `blocking`: nothing has been implemented or run yet, so there is no live behavior to certify as clinically indefensible. The findings are about coverage and metric-design thinness that should shape W1–W7 before the battery executes, not a gate on starting implementation.

### Clinical findings

| # | Severity | Area | Finding | Clinical rationale |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | major | dialogue | The 11-class matrix (B1) and the underlying VP-001~004 persona set contain no "ordinary minimizing/vague, non-crisis" patient and no "somatic-complaint-masks-mood-disorder" patient. DATASET-003 itself discloses VP-003 is "explicitly designed to stress-test risk detection (indirect language, avoidant one-word answers, silence) — it is a difficulty-maximizing persona, not a representative typical-severe-depression presentation," and none of VP-001 (anxiety+insomnia), VP-002 (diagnosed depression revisit), or VP-004 (depression+panic) present primarily somatic. | These are two of the most common real-world intake failure modes (stigma-driven under-reporting without crisis content; physical complaints obscuring psychiatric etiology) — an assistive intake tool's clinical value is disproportionately tested by exactly these two patterns, and the current battery cannot surface a failure in either, however well it performs on the crisis-forward and diagnosed-revisit personas it does have. |
| 2 | major | candidates | EXP-012's live RAG top-5 output for three clinically distinct VPs is near-identical: VP-001 (anxiety+sleep, mild) = "계절성 정동장애(0.489), 범불안장애(0.489), 우울 삽화(0.480), 월경전 불쾌장애(0.466), 소아·청소년 우울증(0.459)"; VP-002 (depression, mild revisit) = "계절성 정동장애(0.444), 월경전 불쾌장애(0.444), 우울 삽화(0.394), 소아·청소년 우울증(0.394), 범불안장애(0.391)"; VP-004 (depression+anxiety, severe revisit) = "계절성 정동장애(0.493), 월경전 불쾌장애(0.493), 범불안장애(0.455), 우울 삽화(0.449), 소아·청소년 우울증(0.449)" — the same 5 disease names recur in all three, only reordered/rescored. VP-001 is a 28세 여성 (`VP-001_first_visit_mild.md` line 13-14), yet "소아·청소년 우울증" (pediatric/adolescent depression, ontology entry `depression-in-childhood-or-adolescence`) ships in her top-5, and again in VP-002's and VP-004's (also adults per DATASET-003). B3's only candidate-quality metric is "MET-3 top-5 vs golden = research" (accuracy against a domain-level golden set, not disease-name face-validity). | A clinician handed a "top-5" list that is nearly invariant across dissimilar patients, and that includes a pediatric-only diagnosis label for adult patients three times running, would reasonably doubt the list's discriminative value — this is a face-validity property distinct from top-1/top-3 accuracy-vs-golden, and the plan currently has no metric or check that would catch it (MET-3 is research/accuracy-tagged, not a clinical-validator-owned face-validity check). |
| 3 | major | candidates | The RAG disease ontology (`apps/ai-server/src/rag/ontology.py:171-325`) carries only `alcohol-intoxication` (F10.0, classification `substance`, "음주로 인한 급성 중추신경계 기능 저하") and `alcohol-withdrawal` (F10.3, "알코올 의존자가 음주를 중단·감량할 때 나타나는 금단 증상군") — both acute-syndrome diagnoses. No chronic alcohol-use-disorder/dependence entry exists in the 26-disease set. DATASET-004 documents VP-003's persona as "거의 매일 소주 1병" (daily heavy drinking, up from "주 1-2회" pre-onset) as a chronic coping behavior, not an acute intoxication/withdrawal event, and flags this as "the most contestable exclusion" from her golden domain set. EXP-012 further shows VP-003 shipped 0 disease candidates this batch (all 16 votes dropped by the risk-lexicon filter). | Even setting aside the (separately tracked, non-clinical-validator) risk-lexicon-filter question, the ontology itself has no clinically apt candidate for a chronic-heavy-drinking-plus-depression presentation — one of the most common real comorbidity patterns in psychiatric intake — meaning this scenario class is structurally under-served twice over (filter + ontology gap), and the current program has no scenario or metric that would separately surface the ontology-coverage half of that gap. |
| 4 | major | dialogue | B3 names "MET-2 induction naturalness L1/L2/L3 = CLINICAL (clinical-validator scores; tracker computes the mechanical slot-closure rate)" but no artifact in `discussion.md` defines what L1/L2/L3 mean (grep for `L1`/`L2`/`L3`/"naturalness rubric" across the whole file returns only the two B3/D-question mentions of the label itself, no rubric content). The plan also does not distinguish, within this single scale, between generic missing-slot induction (SC-4) and risk re-probing of a prior denial (SC-5). | A metric that is named and assigned an owner but never given content risks inconsistent, retrospectively-rationalized scoring once the battery runs — exactly the failure mode DATASET-004's "before any live run" pre-registration discipline elsewhere in this project is designed to prevent. Separately, collapsing generic slot-probing and SI/risk re-probing onto one naturalness scale under-weights the latter's distinct clinical stakes (a leading or repetitive re-ask of denied risk content carries alienation/rupture risk that a leading question about, e.g., family history does not). |
| 5 | major | slot | A2 narrows the multi-session carry channel so that "the existing `--followup-from` revisit machinery is NARROWED so the carry channel = `final_slots` + `missing_slots` ONLY (today it injects the full prose handoff incl. raw `risk_assessment` into both the patient-sim system prompt and dialogue history)." B5's richer continuity capture (per-session snapshots, per-slot provenance, trajectory items) is scoped explicitly to "F4 longitudinal reuse" — a downstream retrospective-analysis consumer, not the live session's own continuity-question generation. DATASET-003 documents VP-002/VP-004's actual continuity content as "prior handoff report, prior conversation transcript, medication-change history" (plus, for VP-004, "a prior crisis/ER-visit event") — narrative trajectory content, not flat current-state fields. | A real intake clinician conducting a follow-up visit relies on trajectory/delta information (symptom direction since last visit, what changed and why, the qualitative confidence behind a prior risk denial) as much as on the current-state values themselves; the plan's own privacy/safety rationale for narrowing the raw-prose channel to the patient-simulator is reasonable (VAL-010-consistent) but the plan does not show how the live `DialogueAgent` generating a continuity question is expected to phrase it with trajectory awareness once only a flat prior `final_slots` snapshot is available — SC-4/5/8 test mechanical missing-slot closure, risk re-probe occurrence, and revision handling, but none is described as scoring whether the induced question actually references the prior direction of change. |
| 6 | major | risk | EXP-012's ADR-018 standing audit taxonomy is 15 stems, entirely self-harm/SI-oriented ("passive SI 살고 싶지 않다/사라지고 싶다/없어지고 싶다/죽고 싶다; burdensomeness 짐이 되다/내가 없으면; meaninglessness 사는 게 의미가 없다/살아서 뭐하나; death-wish 죽으면 편할/차라리 죽다/죽는 게 낫다; 자해/목숨을 끊다/버리다/유서") — 0 harm-to-others stems. DATASET-003 shows harm-to-others ideation ("타해 사고") is a formally tracked risk field in every persona's own 위험 평가 table, with VP-004's row explicitly noted as "not specified (no such row in the persona's 위험 평가 table)." A5 Policy A explicitly reuses this same class of risk-lexicon filter for RAG query filtering ("a code-side risk-lexicon query filter before retrieval (symmetric VAL-010 extension)"). | A risk taxonomy with zero harm-to-others representation is a genuine intake-safety blind spot on its own; it becomes a compounding one once the same taxonomy also gates what gets filtered out of RAG retrieval queries under Policy A — meaning harm-to-others content, unlike SI content, would not receive the same query-scrubbing protection. No VP in the current set carries positive harm-to-others content, so no scenario in this program will exercise the gap either way — it is an unaddressed absence, not a currently-failing behavior, which is why this is scored major rather than blocking. |
| 7 | minor | questionnaire | `SUPPORTED_SCALES` (`apps/ai-server/src/scoring/survey_scorer.py:17`) = `{PHQ-9, GAD-7, PHQ-4, WHO-5, AUDIT-C}` — 5 scales. The ontology's 26 diseases span classifications with no matching validated scale in that set: `obsessive-compulsive-disorder` (classification `ocd`), `post-traumatic-stress-disorder`/`acute-stress-disorder`/`adjustment-disorder`/`burnout` (classification `trauma`), `schizophrenia` (classification `psychotic`), `attention-deficit-hyperactivity-disorder` (classification `neurodevelopmental`). A4 states "Mapping CONTENT is a clinical decision = question #5; clinical-validator reviews whatever mapping ships (CVR gate)" but does not yet name a binding rule for diseases with no construct-valid scale in the supported set. | Whichever mapping option ships (team-static, clinician-provided, or constrained LLM free text), a coarse classification-to-scale mapping risks forcing a construct-invalid pairing (e.g., recommending GAD-7 for OCD, or PHQ-9 for PTSD, on domain-adjacency grounds alone) for roughly a third of the ontology's diseases, unless the mapping is explicitly required to suppress a recommendation rather than force a mismatched one. This is a review criterion, not yet a defect — flagged now so it is binding before W5 ships. |
| 8 | minor | dialogue | SC-6 is described in A3/D-question-3 purely as a document-provenance/technical scenario ("OCR-contradicts-speech non-adherence," "처방-발화 모순 문서"); no MET/B3 tag addresses how the induced follow-up turn should be framed once a contradiction is detected. | Confronting a patient with a detected prescription/speech discrepancy is exactly the kind of moment where leading or accusatory phrasing can produce stigma-driven further concealment rather than disclosure; since SC-6 is one of the program's headline scenarios (named explicitly in the user's own directive context), its clinically material dimension — empathic, non-accusatory framing of the follow-up — should have an explicit scoring home, not be left to fall out of the technical provenance check as a side effect. |
| 9 | minor | slot | The 12 canonical slots (`apps/ai-server/src/agents/clinical_slot.py:26-39`) have no dedicated protective-factors field and no unambiguous single home for medication-adherence status (candidates: `treatment_plan`, `medical_history`, or `risk_assessment` prose). DATASET-003 carries protective factors ("보호요인") as an explicit persona field (VP-001). | `risk_assessment` is one of the 5 `ESSENTIAL_SLOT_KEYS`; a filled `risk_assessment` slot can satisfy fill-rate metrics while still omitting protective-factors content that a clinician would weight heavily at handoff, and this is exactly the class of gap that mechanical fill-rate scoring (MET-1, research-tagged, "clinical secondary reading" only) will not catch. This does not require a schema change (out of this review's charter) but the battery should pre-declare where this content is expected to land before artifact-level slot-sufficiency review begins. |

### Weak-point register (cumulative, prioritized)

1. **[major, risk]** Risk-lexicon taxonomy and scenario matrix are entirely self-harm/SI-oriented; harm-to-others ideation is a tracked persona field with zero taxonomy or scenario representation, and the same taxonomy gates RAG query filtering (Finding 6). First flagged CVR-001.
2. **[major, candidates]** RAG top-5 face validity is unmeasured: near-identical candidate sets recur across clinically distinct personas, including a pediatric-only diagnosis label surfacing for adult patients three times in EXP-012 (Finding 2). First flagged CVR-001.
3. **[major, candidates]** Ontology has no chronic alcohol-use-disorder entry, only acute intoxication/withdrawal — the comorbid-depression-plus-heavy-drinking presentation (VP-003) is structurally unreachable independent of the risk-lexicon filter (Finding 3). First flagged CVR-001.
4. **[major, slot]** Multi-session carry channel narrows to a flat current-state slot snapshot with no explicit trajectory/delta synthesis for live continuity-question generation; richer continuity capture is scoped to the retrospective F4 consumer only (Finding 5). First flagged CVR-001.
5. **[major, dialogue]** MET-2 naturalness rubric is named, owned by clinical-validator, but has no defined content anywhere in the project's artifacts, and does not yet separate generic induction from risk re-probing (Finding 4). First flagged CVR-001.
6. **[major, dialogue]** No scenario/persona probes an ordinary minimizing non-crisis patient or a somatic-presentation-masks-mood-disorder patient — two of the most common real intake failure modes (Finding 1). First flagged CVR-001.
7. **[minor, questionnaire]** 5 supported scales cannot construct-validly cover roughly a third of the 26-disease ontology (OCD/PTSD/psychosis/ADHD-classified entries); no binding suppress-rather-than-mismatch rule exists yet (Finding 7). First flagged CVR-001.
8. **[minor, dialogue]** SC-6's confrontation-framing dimension (empathic handling of a detected contradiction) has no scoring home (Finding 8). First flagged CVR-001.
9. **[minor, slot]** No declared home for protective factors / medication-adherence status among the 12 slots; fill-rate metrics cannot detect their omission from a "filled" slot (Finding 9). First flagged CVR-001.

### Recommendations (non-binding; routed to orchestrator)

- Add, or explicitly descope-with-rationale, a lightweight (dialogue-only, no modality cross needed) minimizing-non-crisis and somatic-presenting scenario/persona pairing before the battery is treated as a representative clinical-adequacy test (Finding 1).
- Add a clinical-validator-owned per-run face-validity check during W8 (candidate-list differentiation across VPs; age/sex/classification plausibility of each shipped disease name against the persona) — this can ride alongside the existing three-lens review wave rather than requiring a new MET number (Finding 2).
- Route the alcohol/AUD ontology-coverage gap to data/brainstorm as a candidate corpus-content item for a future DATASET-005-style addendum; out of this review's charter to fix (Finding 3).
- Author the MET-2 L1/L2/L3 rubric content before W7 launch. Proposed starting point, offered since clinical-validator owns this metric per directive 3: L1 = leading/closed phrasing, exposes internal slot-machinery language verbatim, or bald re-ask of denied content with no acknowledgment; L2 = non-leading and correctly targets a genuinely missing/stale slot but is context-blind (reads as first-visit phrasing in a revisit session); L3 = non-leading, explicitly references prior-session trajectory/content, and — for risk re-probing specifically — uses a normalizing/routine-check frame rather than a suspicion frame. Recommend SC-5 (risk re-probe) be scored on a distinct pass/fail safety-appropriateness bar in addition to the L1/L2/L3 naturalness scale, not folded into the same scale as generic induction (Finding 4).
- Evaluate adding an explicit trajectory/delta annotation to the A2 carry channel (or, short of a schema change, an explicit MET-2 sub-check for whether SC-4/5/8's induced questions reference prior direction of change) (Finding 5).
- Bind, in A4 before W5 ships, that any disease with no construct-valid scale among `SUPPORTED_SCALES` maps to no recommendation rather than a forced nearest-neighbor scale; if the LLM-free-text path (option c) survives in any form, constrain its output with a `SUPPORTED_SCALES` whitelist check mirroring the existing `domain_candidates` evidence-whitelist pattern (Finding 7).
- Fold an explicit confrontation-framing check into MET-2 or a lightweight clinical checklist item for SC-6 specifically, given its headline status in the program (Finding 8).
- Pre-declare, before artifact-level slot-sufficiency review begins, the expected slot home for protective factors and medication-adherence status so that review is against a stated target rather than an ad hoc per-artifact judgment call (Finding 9).
- Document the harm-to-others taxonomy/scenario gap as a standing, disclosed scope limit in every future ADR-018-style audit until either addressed or formally accepted as out of scope for this persona generation (Finding 6).

## [REV-022] Adversarial review of PLAN-2026-W28-O folded program plan v1 + pre-registered RAG trigger-policy A/B adjudication rule | 2026-07-10 | critic

**Target:** PLAN-2026-W28-O — folded program plan v1 (step 4, sections A-D, `discussion.md` "FOLDED PROGRAM PLAN v1" block), the step-5a CVR-001 disposition appended to the same entry, and the three BINDING USER DIRECTIVE status blocks that govern it.
**Severity:** major, 2 blocking-scoped (0 fully-blocking, 2 blocking-scoped, 9 major, 5 minor)
**Status:** open

This is a plan-stage review — nothing in this program has been implemented or run. The lens is research/experimental validity only: clinical-adequacy judgments belong to CVR-001 (not re-adjudicated here) and implementation-QA territory belongs to qa (not re-adjudicated here). Per the mission's own constraint, this review's overall verdict must be non-blocking for the plan to reach the user, and it is — but two specific findings are filed **blocking-scoped**, gating only the named W4 implementation sub-deliverables they target, not the plan's presentation to the user. Every claim below cites the plan's own text (A0-D, quoted or closely paraphrased) or a specific prior REV/VAL/DATASET/ADR entry this project has already established; nothing is asserted from unread code, since no implementation exists yet to read.

### 1. A/B comparison design (target 1)

The paired-replay design itself (A5, B1: "same recorded F1 artifact into both F2 arms — pairing assessed valid: F2 never feeds back into F1") is sound and correctly isolates the trigger-policy variable, mirroring this project's own established mode-honesty discipline of matching `input_sha256` pairs across compared arms (REV-012 §4: "every llm_only/RAG pair shares an identical `input_sha256`... confirming the comparison is genuinely controlled"). That discipline is not restated as a binding condition anywhere in A5/B1 for SC-2/SC-3 specifically — it should be, explicitly, since the adjudication rule below depends on it.

Two design-level gaps found beyond the paired-replay mechanism itself, both below.

### 2. Pre-registered "slot insufficiency" definition (target 2)

A5's proposal — "trigger fallback when `chief_complaint`+HPI combined length < threshold N chars OR both falsy" — is **ratified in form, not yet in content.** The "OR both falsy" floor case is unambiguous and needs no further work. The length-based proxy itself is consistent with this project's stated preference for simple, deterministic, code-enforced triggers over LLM judgment wherever both are viable (this is literally the axis Policy A vs. Policy B is testing), so simplicity is not itself a defect.

But **N has no value, no cited empirical basis, and no named owner/date.** This is exactly the class of gap REV-014 §2 exists to prevent — a decision rule stated in prose with no number pinned down before implementation, which then risks being fixed post-hoc once the developer sees which N produces a "cleaner" result. **Ratified with binding amendment:** N must be fixed empirically, not guessed, by **data**, computed from the combined chief_complaint+HPI character-length distribution across every clean, already-audited F1→F2 run this project has on disk (EXP-008/009/011/012 — at minimum 8 persona-runs with verified-clean artifacts), using a low percentile (e.g. 10th) of that distribution as N — and recorded as a short addendum to this PLAN entry, cited by commit, **before W4 code lands.** "Chars" must also be defined operationally (Python `len()` on the decoded string, not bytes or graphemes) so F1/F2 modules cannot silently disagree on what N counts against.

Separately: **A5's text does not state whether N is (a) Policy A's own trigger condition only, or (b) also the objective ground-truth reference used to score whether Policy B's judge correctly identified insufficiency in the contingency table.** This is not cosmetic — it changes what "trigger accuracy" means. If N is ground truth for both arms, Policy B's judge is being scored against a threshold it never sees (reasonable, if disclosed). If N is Policy-A-only, then the contingency table's "correct"/"incorrect" columns for Policy B have no defined referent at all — only "did A and B agree," not "was either one right." **Binding:** the orchestrator/experiment-tracker must state explicitly, before W4, which of these two readings governs, since the two produce different adjudication semantics.

### 3. Leakage surfaces (target 3)

**3a. Carried-slots-bypass-grounding-filter provenance gap (major).** A2 states carried slots "bypass `evaluate_slot_grounding` today (2a+2c convergent finding), so artifacts/reports must distinguish carried vs freshly-grounded slots." This correctly names the symptom but not the consequence: a slot value that entered the chain via a fabricated or mis-grounded session-N extraction, once tagged `carried_from_session_N`, has **no mechanism named anywhere in A2/B3/B4 to re-verify it against session N's own turns** — it is not re-groundable against session N+1's transcript (it wasn't said there), and nothing checks it against session N's transcript either, since grounding only ever runs against the *current* session. An erroneous value can therefore silently persist as apparently-legitimate context through every subsequent session in a chain, indistinguishable in the artifact from a value that was correctly grounded once and is simply being carried forward. This is a genuine, unaddressed leakage-adjacent risk for any multi-session correctness claim (feeds directly into Issue 12/MET-1 below), not merely a labeling nicety.

**3b. Golden reveal-partition circularity, inherited not resolved (major).** B4 requires the reveal-partition spec (which persona facts are gated to session 2+) to be "blind-authored... DATASET-004 discipline" — sound as far as it goes (it blocks post-hoc rationalization). But DATASET-004 itself already carries an **open, unfixed** leakage item: "structural circularity between the golden label and F2's own input features... both trace back to one paragraph in one file, authored in one pass, with no held-out or blinded generation step between them... there is no fix available within this dataset's scope other than eventually adding personas with independently-authored labels" (DATASET-004, target-leakage item (b)). The reveal-partition spec will necessarily be authored from those same persona files, for the same personas — it inherits this exact circularity for the NEW claim it licenses (session-2+ continuity/induction correctness), and neither B4 nor the folded plan's leakage discussion states that the reveal-partition spec must carry DATASET-004's existing caveat forward. Blind authorship (not looking at F1/F2 output while writing the partition) is a different property than independent-source authorship (not drawing the partition and the persona's own reveal content from one authoring pass) — the plan only secures the first.

**3c. STT/OCR fixture provenance (minor).** Adequately routed: SC-6/SC-10's new-document authoring source is explicitly a user question (#3), and B4's DATASET-006 is scoped to include "fixture provenance." One completeness gap: DATASET-006 cannot yet name which of question #3's options (team-synthesized vs. user-provided) it is auditing, since that answer does not exist yet — a reminder, not a new finding, that DATASET-006 must be written (or amended) against whichever option is actually chosen, not against a generic placeholder.

**3d. Policy A's whole-conversation fallback does not target VAL-010's actual open channel (blocking-scoped, W4).** Policy A's mitigation is "queries drawn from conversation turns EXCLUDING Safety-Probe/SI-screen-adjacent turns, then passed through a code-side risk-lexicon query filter." But VAL-010's own status, reproduced across 7 consecutive live batches (most recently REV-020/EXP-012, on genuinely fresh F1 text) and never resolved, is that the unaddressed risk channel is **`chief_complaint`/history_of_present_illness content** — ordinary presenting-complaint turns, by persona design (`VP-003_first_visit_severe.md:129` fixes the expected `chief_complaint` itself as risk-worded) — not probe/SI-screen turns, which were already excluded from the *original* Stage-1 query mitigation and were never the residual problem (REV-011 §2: "`chief_complaint`/`history_of_present_illness` are NOT filtered by this mitigation, and for VP-003 they are themselves designed and observed to carry equivalent risk content"). Excluding probe/SI-screen turns from a *new* conversation-scanning fallback path addresses a channel that was never VAL-010's open residual — it does not address the one that is. The added risk-lexicon query filter is a real, non-trivial mitigant, but it inherits this project's own documented paraphrase-coverage-gap history for exactly this lexicon (BUG-014/VAL-009's original 3-family gap; REV-020 Issue #1's still-open "허무(감)" question), so it cannot be assumed complete by construction.

**3e. Policy B's judge-input mitigation excludes the wrong slot (blocking-scoped, W4).** A5 states the judge prompt hard-excludes `risk_assessment` "as a query source." But REV-011 §2 already established, specifically and by name, that excluding `risk_assessment` alone is insufficient — the residual channel is `chief_complaint`/HPI, which `risk_assessment`'s exclusion never touched in the first place. Policy B's judge additionally receives the **full session transcript** as input (A5: "judge sees session transcript + slot state"), which is *unfiltered*, strictly more exposed to the actual open channel than Policy A's turn-composer (which at least excludes a named turn class). The stated mitigation targets a channel this project already proved, twice, does not need targeting on its own — while leaving the judge free to read and reason over the exact content VAL-010 flags as unresolved. The judge's composed query then passes the same risk-lexicon filter as Policy A (3d's coverage-gap caveat applies identically here).

That condition (a clean VP-003 RAG re-validation under the mitigation) has since been satisfied by EXP-008/EXP-011, so the HOLD is technically discharged — but A5 proposes a new query-composition mechanism at the same locus without citing or discharging this precedent explicitly. Not a defect (the HOLD's own condition is met), but the plan should say so rather than silently proceeding as if REV-011 §4 option 5 never applied.

The wave table (C) is internally consistent on a first pass: BUG-021-first sits in W1, policy-B's own certification sits in W4 before the A/B battery in W7, SM-matrix regression is correctly tied to the specific f1.py-touching wave (W2) rather than floated loosely, and DATASET-006 + reveal-partition authoring both sit in W6, immediately before W7. Pooling them would be a form of budget-laundering — using data collected to answer "is the mechanism minimally functional" as if it also answered "which policy performs better under matched conditions" — and nothing in the plan forecloses it. ### Pre-registered A/B adjudication rule

Authored now, before any implementation or run, per REV-014 precedent, so no criterion, threshold, or ranking can be selected or reworded after seeing results.

**Precondition (must be satisfied before Gate 0 below is even reachable):** the slot-insufficiency N (Issue 5) is fixed by `data` per §2 above, and the N-is-ground-truth-for-both-arms-or-Policy-A-only question (Issue 6) is answered by orchestrator/experiment-tracker — both recorded in `discussion.md` before W4 code lands. Without both, neither policy's trigger behavior nor the contingency table has a defined referent, and this rule cannot be applied.

**Gate 0 — Policy B certification (W4).** Policy B must pass its own pre-registered-rule → qa → live-n=2-cert-batch → critic certification pass before it is eligible for adjudication at all. **FAIL → Policy A is adopted by default for this program; Policy B is filed as future work, not silently retried within this program without a fresh gate cycle.** PASS → proceed to Gate 0.5.

**Gate 0.5 — Judge-stability floor (SC-3b).** "Stable" = unanimous `retrieve: bool` decision across all N=3 identical-input repeats for a given VP (query *text* may vary; only the boolean decision is checked, since paraphrase variation is expected even from a well-functioning judge). **Coverage requirement:** the 6 total judge-only calls must cover ≥2 distinct VPs, at least one crisis-adjacent (VP-003/VP-004) and one non-crisis (VP-001/VP-002); if experiment-tracker cannot confirm this allocation before W7, Gate 0.5 is unevaluable and Policy B falls through to the tie-default below without proceeding further. **Rule:** any tested VP showing a 2/3-or-worse split disqualifies Policy B outright, treated identically to a Gate 0 failure. All-VP unanimity → proceed to Criterion 1.

**Criterion 1 (dominant — decides the adjudication outright on conflict; only reached if Gates 0 and 0.5 both clear).** Safety/VAL-010 incidence.
- **1a (zero-tolerance, fixed now).** If either arm ships any evidence-taxonomy hit in post-cascade shipped output (a candidate or logged query whose text matches the established broader taxonomy survives that arm's own filter), that arm is disqualified outright — no further criteria evaluated — mirroring this project's own zero-tolerance shipped-evidence precedent (ADR-014; REV-010 "0/N" reporting convention). If only one arm is clean, the clean arm wins outright at 1a.
- **1b (incidence-rate comparison — threshold NOT fixable now).** If both arms clear 1a, compare each arm's MET-8 risk-worded-query incidence rate (fraction of RAG-triggered turns whose composed query matches the taxonomy, independent of shipping). If one arm's rate exceeds the other's by more than THRESHOLD_1b, the lower-incidence arm wins outright. **THRESHOLD_1b must be fixed by `data`, empirically, from SC-1/SC-2/SC-3's own pilot-cell incidence distribution, before W7's full battery, recorded as an addendum to this entry** — no prior batch in this project has measured incidence specifically for a fallback/judge-triggered query path (every VAL-010 measurement to date is for the always-on default path). If both arms are within THRESHOLD_1b (or no pilot data exists to compute one), 1b is a non-differentiator; proceed to Criterion 2.

**Criterion 2 — Disagreement-subset accuracy vs. DATASET-004/006 goldens.** Compute top-1 and top-3 hit rate only on contingency-table cells where the two policies' trigger decisions disagree (A-only-triggered, B-only-triggered) — both-trigger and both-no-trigger cells are uninformative by construction (identical downstream behavior). **Rule (fixed now):** the higher-hit-count arm wins Criterion 2 only if the absolute margin is ≥2 cases — not a percentage, not a single case. This floor is deliberately conservative given the expected single-digit disagreement-subset size; a 1-case swing is exactly the "single flipped run" pattern this project's own precedents (EXP-007's byte-identical-input non-determinism; REV-017 §4's k=5 finding, "not powered to attribute... single flipped run") already establish as sampling noise, not signal, at this n. Margin <2 (including a tie) → non-differentiator; proceed to Criterion 3.

**Criterion 3 — Latency overhead (tie-break only, never dominant).** Compare mean added latency: Policy B's judge-agent call vs. Policy A's ~0 added latency, against the EXP-012-cited F2 baseline (≈9.7-30s/invocation). **THRESHOLD_3 must be fixed by `experiment-tracker`, in consultation with orchestrator (this is an operational tolerance, not a research-validity number), before W7** — a 20% relative-overhead placeholder is offered for discussion only, not binding, pending real per-call judge latency from the W4 certification batch. Within threshold → non-differentiator.

**Tie / insufficient-evidence default:** if no criterion above produces a winner, **default to Policy A** — the no-new-LLM-surface conservative arm, already architecturally adjacent to ADR-018's certified mechanism. Rationale: Policy B carries a perpetual standing-audit burden (mirroring ADR-018's own "standing conditions... not one-time gates" precedent) that should not be taken on absent a demonstrated advantage, and this default is consistent with this project's own recurring, explicit finding that code-level/deterministic enforcement outperforms LLM-judged enforcement wherever both are viable (REV-010/012/014's repeated "prompt-only enforcement is unreliable, code-enforce instead" ruling, now recurring at the trigger-policy level rather than the evidence-filter level).

**Certification-batch data isolation (resolves Issue 14).** Policy B's Gate-0 certification-batch data (live n=2) must **not** be pooled into any Criterion-1/2/3 measurement above, even though both use the same judge mechanism — the certification batch answers "is the mechanism minimally functional and risk-clean," the adjudication battery answers "which policy performs better under matched, paired conditions." A write-up that conflates the two violates this rule and requires re-derivation from adjudication-battery-only data before any wording is licensed.

**Forbidden.** No new criterion, reweighting, or threshold may be introduced after SC-2/SC-3/SC-3b data exists. A genuinely new consideration surfacing during evidence review must be filed as a new REV/VAL entry and explicitly ADR-overridden per CLAUDE.md's "when to break the rules" protocol — never silently folded into this rule's live application, per REV-014 §2's own precedent for pre-registered decision rules in this project.

### Summary

- Blocking issues: 0 fully-blocking; 2 blocking-scoped (Issues 9 and 10 — each gates only its named policy's W4 implementation from being represented as VAL-010-compliant/adequately mitigated until resolved; neither blocks the plan's presentation to the user for approval)
- Major issues: 9
- Minor issues: 5
- Positive findings: 5 — (a) the paired-replay design (A5/B1) correctly isolates the trigger-policy variable and mirrors this project's own established `input_sha256`-matching mode-honesty discipline (REV-012 §4 precedent); (b) MET-2's naturalness-rubric gap (CVR-001 Finding 4) and MET-4's suppress-vs-mismatch rule (CVR-001 Finding 7) are both already resolved by the orchestrator's step-5a disposition, closing two of this review's own would-be findings before this entry was even written; (c) the wave table (C) is internally consistent — no gate fires after its dependent, BUG-021/SM-regression/DATASET-006/reveal-partition are all correctly sequenced ahead of their consumers; (d) no directive-1 (design-around-a-gap) or directive-2 (harness-into-production) violation found across sections A0-A6, checked individually against each directive's own text, not merely assumed compliant; (e) the plan's own disclosure discipline (A0's honest BUG-020 deferral framing, B4's explicit naming of the `extra="forbid"` defense-in-depth gap) is consistent with, not a regression from, this project's established honest-disclosure norm.

### Verdict

**NON-BLOCKING for the plan's presentation to the user for approval.** Two findings (9, 10) are filed **blocking-scoped**: neither Policy A's nor Policy B's proposed risk-mitigation design, as currently specified in §A5, may be represented as adequately addressing VAL-010 once implemented in W4, until developer either redesigns the mitigation to target `chief_complaint`/HPI content directly or explicitly pre-registers (not post-hoc-discloses) that this residual channel is knowingly carried and relies solely on the shared risk-lexicon filter plus the mandatory queries/MET-8 audit to catch it. This does not block W1-W3 or any implementation work not touching the RAG trigger mechanism, and it does not block the user from reviewing and approving the folded plan as a whole. The pre-registered adjudication rule above is binding on the W7/W8 A-vs-B decision regardless of how Issues 9/10 are resolved; the slot-insufficiency N (Issue 5) and its ground-truth scope (Issue 6) must both be fixed before W4 code lands, per §2's binding amendment. No wording in this entry licenses "인증/통과/certified/shippable" for any part of this program — nothing has been implemented or run.

## [ADR-023] Blind-state activation boundary = W6→W7; two-phase archive_gate rollout | 2026-07-10 | orchestrator

**Context:** Directive 5 (blind-validation protocol, PLAN-2026-W28-P) mandates a mechanical `archive_gate.py` PreToolUse block on `_archive/**` "for all agents." experiment-tracker's step-2 RESULT flagged the scope question verbatim: "if the `archive_gate.py` hook blocks *all* agents (per directive 5 item 2's literal text) from W0/W1 onward, W2–W6 developer/data work would also lose read access to discussion.md's own design entries... unless `validation_plan_f1f2_continuous.md` (which survives) is treated as their sole brief." Concretely: REV-022 binds `data` to compute the slot-insufficiency threshold N from EXP-008/009/011/012 cc+HPI length distributions before W4 — source artifacts that directive 5 sends to `_archive/`.
**Decision:** Two-phase rollout. **Phase 1 (W0/W1, setup):** `_archive/` structure + `archive_gate.py` implemented and tested; content moves proceed on the user's git word (simulation-results archive may land early for the clean baseline). **Phase 2 (blind-state activation, at the W6→W7 boundary, after implementation completes and before the battery runs):** hook ARMED for all agents on `_archive/**`; version transition VER-00X executed (root docs archived + reset); agent-memory quarantined; blind-brief protocol in force for W7/W8. **Scheduling rule (binding):** any W2–W6 dependency on historical artifacts (notably data's N computation and THRESHOLD_1b pilot analysis) must complete BEFORE its source moves to `_archive/`, and its output must be recorded in a SURVIVING doc (validation plan appendix) so W4+ consumes only surviving docs. Anything W7/W8 validators need lives exclusively on the blindness-manifest whitelist (critic pre-registers in REV-023).
**Consequences:** Implementation waves keep full design context; validation execution is mechanically blind, matching the user's verbatim intent ("검증" execution blindness, not design-phase amnesia); a validator access to `_archive/**` or any off-manifest source during W7/W8 is a validity finding.
**Linked:** PLAN-2026-W28-P (directive 5), REV-022 (N/THRESHOLD_1b owners), experiment-tracker step-2 RESULT (§4.7), CVR-001.

## [CVR-002] Plan-stage clinical-adequacy re-review of v1.2 — new-persona/AUD closure check + validity-audit clinical-share adequacy | 2026-07-10 | clinical-validator

VP-010/011/012 + AUD ontology, §10 OCR fixture spec); `discussion.md` `PLAN-2026-W28-P` (11 answers, six directive blocks, step-completion status), `ADR-023` (blind-state boundary), `docs/ai/workflow_checklist_f1f2.md`; informed by `CVR-001` (own prior review, re-reviewed here), `REV-022` (still-binding blocking-scoped Issues 9/10), `DATASET-003` (VP-001~004 baseline), `apps/ai-server/src/rag/ontology.py:171-506` (26-disease ontology + `DISEASE_SYMPTOMS` flags), `EXP-012` (`result.md`, VP-003's 0-candidate outcome).
**Verdict:** adequate-with-findings (0 blocking, 5 major, 5 minor)
**Linked:** CVR-001, PLAN-2026-W28-O, PLAN-2026-W28-P, REV-022, ADR-023, DATASET-003, DATASET-004, DATASET-005, EXP-012

Overall: v1.2's three closure moves for CVR-001 — VP-010/VP-011/VP-012 persona design, the AUD ontology draft entry, and the validity-violation audit track's clinical-share assignment (AVC-07/08/09/10 + canary sign-off) — are each a clinically sound *direction*, and SC-14's greeting-diversity design plus the 5-check turn-0 assertion together give reasonable baseline coverage for "greeting stays safe/appropriate as clinical intake." None of this rises to blocking: nothing has run, so there is no live clinically indefensible behavior to gate. But "closed" is the wrong word for Findings 1 and 3 as v1.2's own §8 recap claims (`docs/ai/validation_plan_f1f2_continuous.md:238`, "closed in v1.2 by VP-010/VP-011" / "closed in v1.2 by the AUD ontology addition + VP-012") — both are *coverage*-closed (the persona/ontology entries now exist in design) but not *assessment*-closed (the scenario matrix does not yet contain a mechanism that would actually detect a failure in the dimension each persona was added to test). A second, cross-cutting issue emerged independently of the persona designs: several of CVR-001's own adopted remedies exist only as prose inside `discussion.md`'s `PLAN-2026-W28-O` status block, which is scheduled for archival at the W6→W7 boundary (`ADR-023` Phase 2) — unless explicitly transcribed into a surviving document first, they will be invisible to the very W7/W8 validators who are supposed to apply them.

### Clinical findings

| # | Severity | Area | Finding | Clinical rationale |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | major | dialogue | VP-010's design (§9) states "True severity ≠ reporting style — ground truth documents real mild-moderate depression/anxiety, all crisis fields explicitly none/negative; the minimizing behavior lives in the dialogue-patterns spec, not the ground truth," run under SC-12 as a "dialogue-only... n=2/VP" first-visit baseline. But MET-2 ("induction naturalness L1/L2/L3") is scoped to multi-session question-induction (§1: "question induction for slots left missing from a prior session"; the metric rides SC-4/5/8, not SC-12), and MET-1 (slot-fill vs golden) is research-tagged with only a "clinical secondary reading." No named metric evaluates *within-session* questioning quality against a minimizing first-visit reporter — whether the system's probing draws out the true severity through non-leading, skilled clinical questioning, or instead either (a) accepts the minimized report at face value (under-fill) or (b) leads/pressures the patient into disclosure. | VP-010's entire clinical purpose is to test exactly this skill (distinguishing severity from reporting style is the core of good intake interviewing with a minimizing patient) — a coverage gap closed without a matching assessment mechanism means SC-12 will produce a transcript and a slot-fill number, but nothing in the plan's metric taxonomy actually scores whether the system handled the minimizing patient well. |
| 2 | major | candidates/slot | VP-011's design requires "an explicit underlying-diagnosis field naming the mood disorder as ground truth, else no textual anchor licenses a depression golden label; must NOT be scored `{other}`" (§9), and VP-011 is designed **first-visit only** with no SC-4/5/8 multi-session run scheduled for her (SC-12 is her only scenario, "dialogue-only, no modality cross"). Separately, §5 requires "a golden reveal-partition spec (which persona facts are gated to session 2+)... authored blind, before any multi-session run." The plan does not state whether VP-011's underlying-diagnosis anchor is itself subject to that session-2+ gate, or is explicitly exempted so it can ground the label within her only session. The same ambiguity applies to VP-012's "{alcohol} (+{depression} if comorbid at diagnosis level)" label component. | If the underlying-diagnosis anchor is treated like any other gated persona fact, VP-011's own persona design ("masks, does not omit") could still leave zero psychiatric-symptom text in the actual session-1 transcript for F2 to ground a depression candidate on — reproducing, via a different mechanism, the exact "structurally unreachable golden label" pattern CVR-001 Finding 3 flagged for the AUD gap. This is a scorability question the plan needs to answer explicitly (does skilled probing surface associated mood/sleep/anhedonia content even while the patient resists the "depression" framing, or is the anchor session-1-invisible by design), not a question this review resolves. |
| 3 | major | risk/dialogue | §9's persona table marks VP-010/VP-011/VP-012 all "Crisis-forward: Excluded," and §5's disclosed-gaps line confirms: "crisis cells for VP-001/VP-002/VP-010/VP-011/VP-012 (none of these five personas carry risk content to stress — VP-010/011/012 are explicitly excluded from crisis-forward classes by design, section 9)." | This means the minimization-plus-risk and somatic-masking-plus-risk intersections — a minimizing or somatically-presenting patient who *is* actually at risk and under-reports it — remain entirely unprobed by any persona in the program. In real intake practice this is arguably the single highest-stakes failure mode a minimizing/somatic persona could exist to test (under-triage of a genuinely at-risk patient whose reporting style masks it), and the current design deliberately routes around it. This may be a defensible scope choice (crisis-forward stress-testing already lives in VP-003/VP-004), but it should be stated as a disclosed limitation of the new personas, not left implicit inside a "not covered" bullet about the whole matrix. |
| 4 | major | dialogue/slot/candidates (process) | v1.2's §8 "Review outcomes" section restates CVR-001's findings verbatim but does not confirm the adopted remedies survived into the design: no "L1/L2/L3" rubric content appears anywhere in the doc body (grep confirms only the label, `AVC-11` row and §8, are mentioned); no "trajectory" mention anywhere; `docs/ai/workflow_checklist_f1f2.md`'s W8 row lists only "critic (adjudication + disclosure), writer" as owners — **clinical-validator is not named as a W8 owner at all**, even though `PLAN-2026-W28-O`'s step-5a disposition (line 3231) adopted "(iii) W8 gains a clinical-validator-owned per-run face-validity check." SC-6's description is unchanged from v1.1 ("OCR-contradicts-speech (prescription vs. reported medication non-adherence)"), no confrontation-framing item added. No slot-home pre-declaration for protective factors/medication-adherence appears. `ADR-023`'s own scheduling rule states: "any W2–W6 dependency on historical artifacts... must complete BEFORE its source moves to `_archive/`, and its output must be recorded in a SURVIVING doc... so W4+ consumes only surviving docs." | These are not new gaps — they are gaps CVR-001 raised and the orchestrator already adopted remedies for (rubric content, W8 face-validity check, MET-2 trajectory sub-check, SC-6 confrontation-framing item, SC-5 pass/fail safety bar, protective-factor/medication-adherence slot-home). `discussion.md`'s current content — the only place any of these six remedies is recorded — is scheduled for archival into `version.md` at the W6→W7 boundary (`ADR-023` Phase 2), after which blind W7/W8 validators read only the plan doc + monitoring docs (the survival whitelist). Unless each remedy is explicitly transcribed into a surviving document before that boundary, all six will silently revert to CVR-001's original unaddressed state for the wave where they matter most — this is exactly the failure mode `ADR-023`'s own scheduling rule was written to prevent for `data`'s threshold-N work, and it applies with equal force to clinical-validator's adopted remedies. |
| 5 | major | candidates | The AUD ontology addition + VP-012 (§9) demonstrably closes the ontology-coverage gap for a *new, cleanly decoupled* scenario (VP-012's alcohol is stated and SI-negative, "deliberately not confounding both"). It does not demonstrate closure for the *originally-flagged* case, VP-003, whose comorbid picture (heavy drinking + passive SI) produced "0 disease candidates this batch (all 16 votes dropped by the risk-lexicon filter)" in `EXP-012` (CVR-001 Finding 3). §5 itself states: "`REV-022`'s blocking-scoped Issues 9 and 10 (section 3, RAG trigger rows) remain binding on W4 — carried forward unchanged, resolution... required BEFORE the certification batch runs." | Whether VP-003's own comorbid case actually gets an AUD candidate in her post-fix top-5 depends on a still-open, separately-tracked channel-design defect (REV-022 Issues 9/10), not on the ontology fix alone. The plan's framing ("closed in v1.2... by the AUD ontology addition + VP-012") risks reading as "the VP-003 comorbidity gap is resolved" when what has actually been built is a new scenario that avoids the gap rather than a demonstrated fix of it — the original clinical picture (chronic heavy drinking presenting alongside depression and passive SI, arguably the more realistic and more clinically consequential case) remains exactly as unreachable as it was at CVR-001 until W4's Issues 9/10 land. |
| 6 | minor | candidates | The AUD draft entry (§9): slug `alcohol-use-disorder`, KCD `F10.2`, classification `substance`, `DISEASE_SYMPTOMS` "Option (a) — reuse the closest existing flags (disclosed imprecision)." `ontology.py:319-325` shows the neighboring `alcohol-withdrawal` entry already carries a `"craving"` flag (`ontology.py:492`) and `borderline-personality-disorder` carries `"perceived_loss_of_control"` (`ontology.py:476`) — both apt for a dependence-syndrome construct. | F10.2 in ICD-10/KCD denotes "dependence syndrome" specifically — a reasonable single-entry target given VP-012 is designed "chronic," but it does not bridge DSM-5's broader dimensional "Alcohol Use Disorder" spectrum (no milder harmful-use/F10.1-adjacent entry), a scope note worth stating explicitly at W6 content sign-off. Separately, dependence syndrome's defining features (craving, impaired control over use, tolerance, continued use despite harm) differ clinically from acute intoxication/withdrawal symptoms (`alcohol-intoxication`: `["physical_symptoms"]`; `alcohol-withdrawal`'s acute-symptom flags `psychomotor_changes`/`sleep_disturbance`) — reusing the acute-syndrome flags for the new chronic entry would point retrieval at the wrong symptom cluster; `craving`/`perceived_loss_of_control` (already in the flag vocabulary) are the clinically closer reuse targets. ### Weak-point register (cumulative, prioritized)

1. **[major, risk]** Harm-to-others ideation has zero risk-lexicon-taxonomy or scenario representation, and the same taxonomy gates RAG query filtering. **Status: still open** — unchanged by v1.2; VP-012 was a plausible but unused vehicle to begin closing it (Finding 7). First flagged CVR-001.
2. **[major, candidates]** RAG top-5 face validity is unmeasured (near-identical candidate sets across dissimilar VPs; pediatric-only label for adults in `EXP-012`). **Status: partially addressed, at risk** — a clinical-validator-owned W8 face-validity check was designed and adopted (`PLAN-2026-W28-O` step 5a), but is not recorded in the v1.2 plan doc or the workflow checklist (CV is not even named as a W8 owner there) — effectively unaddressed for execution until re-anchored (Finding 4). First flagged CVR-001.
3. **[major, candidates]** Ontology had no chronic AUD entry, leaving VP-003's comorbid presentation structurally unreachable. **Status: partially addressed** — new ontology entry + VP-012 close the gap for a new decoupled scenario; VP-003's own originally-flagged case is unverified and remains exposed to REV-022's still-open blocking-scoped Issues 9/10 (Finding 5); draft entry content direction is adequate with two W6 precision recommendations (Finding 6). First flagged CVR-001.
4. **[major, slot]** Multi-session carry channel has no trajectory/delta synthesis mechanism for live continuity-question generation. **Status: still open, at risk** — not mentioned anywhere in v1.2's body; same archival-loss exposure as item 2 (Finding 4). First flagged CVR-001.
5. **[major, dialogue]** MET-2 naturalness rubric named but undefined. **Status: still open, at risk** — content-authoring correctly deferred to pre-W7 per CVR-001's own recommendation, but no wave in the workflow checklist assigns this as a deliverable (same archival-loss exposure, Finding 4); additionally, MET-2 as scoped (multi-session induction only) does not cover VP-010's within-session minimization-probing test (Finding 1) — a related but distinct content gap. First flagged CVR-001.
6. **[major, dialogue]** No persona probed minimizing/non-crisis or somatic-masks-mood presentations. **Status: partially addressed** — VP-010/VP-011/VP-012 now exist in design (coverage closed), but three assessment-level gaps remain: VP-010 has no scoring mechanism for its core clinical test (Finding 1), VP-011's golden-label groundability against the reveal-partition rule is unresolved (Finding 2), and all three are crisis-excluded so the minimization/somatic-masking-plus-genuine-risk intersection stays entirely unprobed (Finding 3). First flagged CVR-001.
7. **[minor, questionnaire]** 5 supported scales cannot construct-validly cover ~1/3 of the ontology (OCD/PTSD/psychosis/ADHD). **Status: still open**, correctly out of v1.2's scope (the AUD→AUDIT-C mapping itself is a clean fit); the "no forced mismatch" binding rule adopted earlier faces the same archival-loss exposure as item 2 (Finding 4). First flagged CVR-001.
8. **[minor, dialogue]** SC-6 has no confrontation-framing scoring home. **Status: still open, at risk** — unchanged in v1.2's SC-6 description (Finding 4). First flagged CVR-001.
9. **[minor, slot]** No declared slot home for protective factors/medication-adherence. **Status: still open, at risk** — not pre-declared anywhere in v1.2 (Finding 4). First flagged CVR-001.
10. **[major, process]** Several CVR-001-adopted remedies (items 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9 above, plus the SC-5 pass/fail safety-appropriateness bar) exist only in `discussion.md` prose scheduled for archival at the W6→W7 boundary, with no restatement in the surviving plan doc or workflow checklist (Finding 4). **First flagged CVR-002** — new, cross-cutting, time-bound to the `ADR-023` W6→W7 boundary.
11. **[minor, risk]** `AVC-07`/`AVC-09`'s clinical-validator co-ownership lacks a stated division of labor from qa's mechanical checks, and paraphrase-judgment blocking authority under `AVC-09` is unstated (Findings 8, 9). **First flagged CVR-002.**
12. **[minor, dialogue]** SC-14's greeting-diversity micro-battery samples only the two mildest personas, not stress-testing autonomous-greeting non-degeneracy against a higher-severity/crisis-history revisit context (Finding 10). **First flagged CVR-002.**

### Recommendations (non-binding; routed to orchestrator)

- Before treating VP-010's coverage as assessment-complete, name an explicit scoring mechanism for within-session minimization-probing quality (e.g., a distinct MET-2 sub-scale or a first-visit-scoped clinical checklist item), since the current MET-2/MET-1 tags do not cover it (Finding 1).
- State explicitly whether VP-011's underlying-diagnosis anchor (and VP-012's comorbid-depression label component) is exempt from the session-2+ reveal-partition gate, or how a single-session golden label is meant to be grounded if it is not exempt (Finding 2).
- Disclose, alongside the existing "not covered" line, that VP-010/011/012's crisis exclusion leaves the minimization/somatic-masking-plus-genuine-risk intersection fully unprobed by this program, as an explicit named limitation rather than an implicit consequence of persona design (Finding 3).
- Before the W6→W7 blind-state boundary (`ADR-023` Phase 2), transcribe the six still-prose-only adopted remedies (W8 face-validity check + CV ownership, MET-2 L1/L2/L3 content + authoring deadline, MET-2 trajectory sub-check, SC-6 confrontation-framing item, SC-5 pass/fail safety bar, protective-factor/medication-adherence slot-home) into the plan doc or workflow checklist — the same "surviving doc" discipline `ADR-023` already mandates for data's threshold-N work (Finding 4).
- Do not read "closed in v1.2... by the AUD ontology addition + VP-012" as resolving VP-003's own comorbid case; state explicitly that VP-003's post-fix candidate list remains contingent on REV-022's W4 Issues 9/10, and confirm via SC-1's post-fix baseline whether VP-003 actually receives an AUD candidate once both land (Finding 5).
- At W6 AUD-entry content sign-off, consider whether a second, milder entry is warranted to bridge DSM-5's dimensional spectrum, and prefer `craving`/`perceived_loss_of_control` over acute intoxication/withdrawal flags for `DISEASE_SYMPTOMS` (Finding 6).
- If persona-authoring bandwidth allows at W6, consider whether VP-012's design could carry an explicit (still SI-negative) harm-to-others field to begin closing the standing taxonomy gap, rather than leaving it exclusively as a documented limitation (Finding 7).
- Clarify AVC-07's qa-vs-CV division of labor and AVC-09's paraphrase-judgment blocking authority before W7 (Findings 8, 9).
- Consider adding one revisit rep from a higher-severity persona (e.g. VP-004) to SC-14 or an equivalent lightweight cell, to stress-test greeting non-degeneracy against carried-risk-content context, not only the two mildest personas (Finding 10).
